facts.value: The BA programme in American Studies at Goethe University focuses on the literature, culture, and history of the USA. Literary texts and non-literary cultural productions and media (such as film) as well as historical sources are analyzed and discussed in their various contemporary and historical dimensions. This opens up perspectives on different actors, environments, institutions, as well as cultural phases, social developments, and historical and political decisions – from the colonial period to the 21st century. Students acquire expertise in the intercultural dimensions of American literatures, cultures, and American history and develop an understanding of interdisciplinary perspectives on their subject of study and various theoretical approaches and methods.
In Frankfurt, the programme is divided into three main focuses: American Literature and Literary Studies, American Culture and Cultural Studies, and American History and Society.
Institute for English and American Studies (IEAS)

The American Studies department at IEAS is one of the few interdisciplinary American Studies departments in Germany. This orientation is reinforced by close cooperation with other institutes at Goethe University.

Due to the research interests of professors and staff, specific focuses in teaching include certain literary epochs or specific literary and media forms, approaches such as African-American Studies, Gender and Queer Studies, Animal Studies, Film Studies, Sound Studies, Media Philosophy, Aesthetics of Democracy, or the history of the Civil Rights Movement.
From the 3rd semester onwards, students specialize in two of the three offered focuses and begin to develop their own profile.

The IEAS has a long-established theatre group (Chaincourt Theatre Company) and an annually published student anthology featuring texts, poems, and photographs, both of which are operated in close collaboration between teachers and students. These forms of extracurricular engagement provide students with the opportunity to gain initial practical experience in creative professions.
